nodes.name: Manual Run
nodes.notes: On-demand run for backfills, demos and CLI execution. Same path as the schedule.

parameters.query:
-- Open the run ledger entry. Same shared table, source='kpi-refresh'.
--
-- The window is the span of sales dates the rebuild will cover, so the ledger
-- answers "which dates did this refresh account for?" without reading kpi_daily.
WITH span AS (
    SELECT min(order_date) AS from_date, max(order_date) AS to_date
    FROM salesops.fact_orders
)
INSERT INTO salesops.ingestion_runs
    (batch_id, source, window_from, window_to, status, n8n_execution_id)
SELECT
    gen_random_uuid(),
    'kpi-refresh',
    COALESCE((SELECT from_date FROM span), CURRENT_DATE),
    COALESCE((SELECT to_date   FROM span), CURRENT_DATE),
    'running',
    $1
RETURNING
    batch_id::text    AS batch_id,
    window_from::text AS window_from,
    window_to::text   AS window_to,
    run_id;

nodes.name: Rebuild KPI Daily

parameters.query:
-- Full deterministic rebuild of kpi_daily.
--
-- The DELETE and the INSERT live inside salesops.refresh_kpi_daily() rather
-- than in two n8n nodes, because they must be atomic. A function body runs in
-- the caller's transaction, so a failure rolls back the DELETE too and the
-- previous contents survive. Two nodes would leave a window in which kpi_daily
-- was empty, and any reader in that window would see a warehouse with no
-- history.
--
-- Rebuilding wholesale rather than incrementally is a deliberate choice: the
-- table is one row per trading day, so a rebuild is cheaper than the
-- bookkeeping an incremental strategy would need - and it cannot drift from
-- fact_orders.
SELECT * FROM salesops.refresh_kpi_daily();

nodes.notes: Calls salesops.refresh_kpi_daily(). Atomic full rebuild - never half-written.

nodes.name: Finalize KPI Refresh Run

parameters.query:
-- Close the run.
--
-- 'partial' means "completed, but the result is not fully trustworthy": here,
-- at least one date still has orders with no exchange rate, so its money
-- columns are understated. The run genuinely succeeded - the DATA is
-- incomplete - and conflating the two would either hide the gap or cry wolf.
--
-- records_received = dates considered, records_accepted = KPI rows written.
-- They are equal by construction (one row per date), which satisfies the
-- counts-balance CHECK on ingestion_runs.
UPDATE salesops.ingestion_runs r
SET finished_at       = now(),
    records_received  = $2::int,
    records_accepted  = $2::int,
    records_rejected  = 0,
    records_duplicate = 0,
    status            = CASE WHEN $3::int > 0 THEN 'partial' ELSE 'success' END
WHERE r.batch_id = $1::uuid
RETURNING
    run_id,
    batch_id::text AS batch_id,
    status,
    records_accepted AS kpi_dates_written,
    $3::int          AS kpi_dates_incomplete,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM salesops.kpi_daily)::int          AS kpi_rows_total,
    (SELECT min(calendar_date) FROM salesops.kpi_daily)     AS earliest_date,
    (SELECT max(calendar_date) FROM salesops.kpi_daily)     AS latest_date,
    (SELECT round(avg(fx_completeness_pct), 2) FROM salesops.kpi_daily) AS avg_fx_completeness_pct,
    round(extract(epoch FROM (finished_at - started_at))::numeric, 2)   AS duration_seconds;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ [ $('Open KPI Refresh Run').first().json.batch_id, $('Rebuild KPI Daily').first().json.dates_written || 0, $('Rebuild KPI Daily').first().json.dates_incomplete || 0 ] }}

nodes.notes: 'partial' when any date still lacks full FX coverage.
